:::{#lem-gradient-linear-approximation}
#### The linear approximation of the gradient uses the Hessian

Let $f$, $\vx$, the gradient $\vecf{g}$ and the [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) $\matr{H}$ be as in the [quadratic model](#def-quadratic-model),
and let the second partial derivatives of $f$ be [continuous](vector-calculus.qmd#def-continuous-several) on an [open ball](vector-calculus.qmd#def-ball) around $\vx$.
Then the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) of $f$ at $\vx$ is the gradient plus the Hessian times the step:

$$
\vecf{\ell}(\stepvec) = \vecf{g} + \matr{H} \stepvec.
$$ {#eq-gradient-linear-approximation-hessian}

:::

::: proof

For each $i$ and $j$,
the $i$th entry of $\deriv{\vx} \paren{\deriv{x_j} f(\vx)}$ is $\deriv{x_i} \paren{\deriv{x_j} f(\vx)}$,
which is $\sb{\matr{H}}_{ij}$ by the definitions of the [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) and of the [derivative of a vector-valued function](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-valued-derivative).
So, for each $j$,

$$
\ba
\sb{\vecf{\ell}(\stepvec)}_j
&= \deriv{x_j} f(\vx) + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \sb{\matr{H}}_{ij}\,\step_i
&& \text{(@eq-gradient-linear-approximation, as a sum)}
\\
&= \sb{\vecf{g}}_j + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \sb{\matr{H}}_{ij}\,\step_i
&& \text{(definition of } \vecf{g} \text{)}
\\
&= \sb{\vecf{g}}_j + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \sb{\matr{H}}_{ji}\,\step_i
&& \text{(} \matr{H} \text{ is symmetric)}
\\
&= \sb{\vecf{g}}_j + \sb{\matr{H} \stepvec}_j
&& \text{(matrix-vector product)}
\\
&= \sb{\vecf{g} + \matr{H} \stepvec}_j.
&& \text{(vector addition)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-gradient-linear-approximation-entry}

The third line uses the [symmetry of the Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#thm-hessian-symmetric),
which holds because the second partial derivatives are continuous near $\vx$.

:::
